items.title: Scammers Are Posing as Computer 'Rescue' Companies — Don't Pay Them a Dime
items.summary: Crooks are now posing as computer "rescue" companies to steal money. Researchers say a group calling itself Ransom Busters has been emailing people right after their computers are attacked — sometimes before the attack is even public — and offering to "recover" their files for a fee. Researchers believe the "rescuers" are the same crooks behind the attacks. If you get an email or call like this, don't pay, don't reply, and don't call the number in the message. Real help never comes from a stranger demanding money.

items.title: Hackers found a way into Macs over the internet and are using them to mine digital money — update macOS today
items.summary: Open System Settings, click General, then Software Update, and install whatever Apple offers — it's free and takes about 10 minutes. If you can't update right away, you can also turn off Screen Sharing (System Settings → General → Sharing → Screen Sharing) unless you actually use it.

items.title: Your PC feels slow? Task Manager shows what's eating it — built into Windows, press Ctrl+Shift+Esc
items.summary: Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager — it's built into Windows and shows every program running on your computer. Look at the top of the list: whatever is using the most working memory is usually the troublemaker. To close a stuck program, click it, then click End Task.

items.title: Hackers Are Breaking Into Windows Computers Right Now — Update Today
items.summary: The federal government's cyber-watchdog agency warned Wednesday that hackers are actively breaking into Windows computers through a weakness Microsoft already fixed back in April. If your computer hasn't installed the update, a crook can get in over the internet — no clicking, no tricking you — and take it over. The fix takes two minutes: press the Start button, type "check for updates," open it, install whatever it finds, then turn your computer off and back on.

items.title: Firefox just shipped its August 18 security update — check yours free at firefox.com in 2 minutes
items.summary: Open Firefox, click the three-line menu in the top corner, choose Help then About Firefox, and let it finish updating — it's free and takes about 2 minutes. If it says "Firefox is up to date," you're good. If you don't have Firefox at all, download it free from firefox.com.

items.title: Your computer has a check-engine light hidden inside — read it free with CrystalDiskInfo before it quits on you
items.summary: Download CrystalDiskInfo free from crystalmark.info and open it. The big box at the top shows your computer's storage health — think of it as the check-engine light for the part that holds all your files. If it says "Good," you're fine. If it says "Caution" or "Bad," don't wait — bring the computer in and we'll save what we can while there's still time.

items.title: Fake 'Download' Pages Can Take Over Your Browser — Never Copy-Paste From a Website
items.summary: A new bad program called AmnesiaStealer is spreading through fake "download" pages. The page tells you to copy a command and paste it — and once it's in, it takes over the program you use to go on the internet and can steal your saved passwords. Real download pages never ask you to copy and paste commands. If one does, close the tab. Only download programs from the maker's real website, and keep your computer's free updates turned on.

items.title: Internet down? Check the free Xfinity Outage Map before you blame your equipment — xfinity.com/support/statusmap
items.summary: When your internet drops, first check whether the whole neighborhood is down. Open the Xfinity Outage Map at xfinity.com/support/statusmap, type in your service address, and it shows you if there's an outage and when it's expected back. If the map shows nothing, the trouble is inside your house — that's when you call the shop.

items.title: Can't open that file your bank or lawyer sent? 7-Zip opens it free — download at 7-zip.org
items.summary: Files that end in .zip or .rar are just folders squeezed into one file — and Windows won't open all of them. Download 7-Zip free from 7-zip.org, install it (takes about a minute), then right-click the file and choose "7-Zip > Extract here" to get your documents out.

items.title: Crooks Are Buying Expired Websites — a Site You Save Could Become a Trap
items.summary: Crooks are buying up expired website addresses — spending millions to do it — and turning them into traps that install bad programs or run scams. Every day, thousands of website addresses lapse, and security researchers say criminals snap them up to fool people who've trusted those sites for years. If a familiar website suddenly looks different, begs you to install something, or flashes alarming pop-ups, close it. Type the company's address yourself instead, and never click a link that pushes you to a site.

items.title: Your info leaked? Freeze your credit free at Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion
items.summary: A credit freeze stops crooks from opening credit cards or loans in your name — and it's free by federal law. Do it online at equifax.com, experian.com, and transunion.com; it takes about 20 minutes total, and you can freeze a child's credit too.

items.title: Email says 'file too big'? WeTransfer sends it free — no account needed at wetransfer.com
items.summary: Go to wetransfer.com, add your file (up to 3 GB free), type the person's email address, and hit send — they get a link to download it. No account, no software, works in any browser.
